items.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018
items.q: the band director and the repertoire there was usually stuff like Count Basie, you know repertoire kind of standardized high school jazz repertoire

ctx.x: Do you recall what arrangements, what was the style back then?

You know they did a lot of — the band director and the repertoire there was usually stuff like Count Basie, you know repertoire kind of standardized high school jazz repertoire, repertoire maybe a Thad Jones thing would sneak in, but mostly Basie kind of, that kind

of stuff. And that moment, the other component of that experience at that moment was he was improvising. He was taking a solo. And it just had meaning to me. And then ever since then everything I do, and I mean I’m an ensemble player as well, but my kind of my motivation, my fuel for practicing is so that I can exist in the landscape of improvisation you know. But yeah, so that moment, I’ll never forget it, I’ll never forget that picture there of standing there with all these other students and just having that,…
